Responses provider adapters and images

Per-provider Responses behavior: Claude failures and CLI prompt cache, Codex subscription login refresh, Copilot live sessions, the Anthropic API route, and image inputs.

About 14 min read · 6 sections

On this page
01 Service tiers and flex per provider 02 Claude adapter failures and rate limits 03 Codex subscription login refresh 04 Copilot sessions and cancellation 05 Ordinary Anthropic API 06 Images

Part of Responses support. Selecting an inbound protocol does not select an upstream provider; these are the behaviors that belong to one inference route. The shared request contract is on Responses protocol, streaming, and failures and the tool rules on Responses tools across routes.

Service tiers and flex per provider

Flex depends on the provider. The Codex subscription path passes flex through to the upstream, and the model's declared tier list does not apply to it, as in native Codex; the ordinary Responses API provider forwards it the same way. Claude and Copilot run flex as Standard (see their sections below). The Anthropic API and Chat Completions providers ignore every service tier.

Claude subscription requests map priority (or fast) to the CLI's fast mode setting (--settings {"fastMode":true}) when the model's catalog row offers Fast; flex has no Claude equivalent, so it runs the turn as Standard with no fast mode setting; any other tier the model does not offer (scale, an unknown name) is rejected before the CLI starts. The CLI reports its fast mode state. When fast mode stays on, the completion reports priority. When Claude refuses it (for example, no usage credits) and falls back to standard speed, the turn still completes and reports default.

Claude adapter failures and rate limits

Native Claude assistant.error discriminants identify subscription rate limits, authentication, billing, and server failures before an opaque result is handled. Billing refusals report: "Claude billing or extra-usage credits are unavailable. Check your Claude billing settings and payment method, then retry." The gateway also recognizes bounded, known credit-refusal messages inside native failure results when the CLI omits its billing discriminant. These failures are final insufficient_quota errors, so Codex does not repeatedly retry a charge that needs account action. The gateway never returns the provider's private refusal text or guesses whether a card was declined for insufficient funds. Ordinary successful assistant text and an unexplained disconnection do not establish a billing failure. In particular, is_error: true with subtype: success is not successful inference. The CLI reports every 429 as rate_limit, including a transient subscriber capacity throttle ("not your usage limit"). Only a rate_limit_event with status rejected earlier in the same request proves a subscription limit; that becomes a clear, final usage-limit failure. Any other Claude rate limit is a retryable rate_limit_exceeded, so Codex retries it as it did before usage limits became final. Neither is routed to another account automatically. Unknown result subtypes remain bounded diagnostic metadata; private error text is never returned or logged. The native rate_limit_event supplies the affected five-hour or weekly window and reset timestamp. A rate-limit failure includes that provider-reported time in the inference host's local timezone and UTC. Missing metadata remains unknown; the gateway does not guess a reset or retry across a subscription limit. Claude replays public reasoning summaries as explicitly identified historical summary items, separate from ordinary assistant messages. Their readable text is preserved; the gateway does not invent thinking blocks or native signatures. Encrypted reasoning transport state is not exposed to the Claude model. Hosted tools are outside the current Claude adapter's scope. Unsupported item and tool types return a client error instead of an internal crash.

Codex subscription login refresh

A Codex subscription request whose token refresh fails on the network, with an unreadable or malformed reply, or with any HTTP error status other than 400, 401 or 403 (for example a 429 or a 5xx, often right after the Mac wakes) returns a retryable upstream_unavailable, so Codex reconnects instead of ending the chat. Only a missing login, a stored login without a refresh token, an unreadable credential file, a stored login or refresh reply without the plan scopes, or a refresh rejected with HTTP 400, 401 or 403 reports "ChatGPT provider requires login". When the token endpoint names a reason, the message adds its OAuth error code. A rejected login reads "ChatGPT provider requires login (refresh rejected: refresh_token_reused)" and a temporary failure reads "ChatGPT login refresh failed temporarily (temporarily_unavailable); retry shortly". A code outside the fixed list shows as other, and a reply without a code adds nothing. request_failed telemetry records the same code (see docs/diagnostics.md); only the code is kept, and the reply's description, body and tokens are never recorded or shown. A failed refresh is not retried inside the request, because a second token request could spend the single-use refresh token again; Codex reconnects on the retryable 503 instead.

The refresh token is single-use, so only a real request or an explicit gateway discover ever spends it. The six-hour model-metadata refresh never refreshes the Codex login: whenever serving the Codex access token would need a refresh (it has expired, or it is within two minutes of expiring unless the issuer's earliest_refresh_at has not passed yet), that provider is skipped for the round (model_metadata_skipped) without any network call, and the next real request refreshes it. This keeps a refresh from being started while the Mac is asleep, where the reply can be lost after the token was spent. Claude and Copilot discovery in the same refresh still run their own CLI or SDK, which may refresh its own login; guarding them is left to a later release. When a refresh reply arrives, any replacement refresh token is written to the credential file (atomically, mode 0600) in the same save that records the outcome, so a reply that fails a check never loses the rotated token. How the reply is handled:

  • A valid reply that omits scope (or sends null) keeps the scope granted earlier (RFC 6749 sections 5.1 and 6) and is used normally; a scope that is present but not a string counts as malformed.
  • A reply whose scope lacks the plan scopes can only be fixed by signing in again (gateway login ID with plan usage enabled). The gateway keeps the old access token and only the scopes that reply granted, so that request and every later one report "ChatGPT provider requires login" without another token request, in this process or another one waiting on the refresh lock.
  • A malformed reply (no bearer access token or no positive lifetime) is temporary, whatever its scope says, and is checked before the plan scopes. The request returns the retryable upstream_unavailable, the stored access token, scopes and expiry stay as they were, and the next real request refreshes again with the saved replacement token, or with the stored one when the reply carried none.
  • A valid reply without a replacement refresh token is used. The new access token is saved and the stored refresh token stays, because a server may keep a refresh token instead of rotating it (RFC 6749 section 6).

Copilot sessions and cancellation

Copilot uses the same normalized text and replay contract. It registers native SDK custom tools and returns their real calls before any execution. SDK reasoning summaries stream separately; auto requests a concise summary. The adapter rejects BYOK usage, unexpected model/provider changes, host permission requests, foreign tools, inconsistent final text, unsupported SDK versions, and incomplete turns. By default the thread keeps one live CLI session, and a request sends only the items that are new; see live Copilot sessions. Cancelling a live request aborts its session and kills its CLI process (about 2 seconds: the abort is bounded to 2 seconds, then the CLI is killed and its folder removed); the request hands over the usage the CLI reports meanwhile and then ends. The next request starts a new session and sends the caller-supplied history once. Cancelling a one-shot request stops its CLI process and waits for it to exit; a process outside the CLI's group that keeps its output open delays that by half a second of silence on the CLI's output, or by at most about 5 seconds (100 ticks) when output keeps arriving, after which the gateway closes its pipes. Either way, usage the CLI reported before the cancellation, or reports while it is being aborted, still reaches the usage ledger and telemetry. Anonymous first questions, explicit compaction/prewarm/memory requests and explicitly selected one-shot mode use standalone sessions. Capacity, concurrent work, startup, delivery and live-stream failures return a final refusal instead of automatic replay. Historical anonymous conversations require a caller conversation ID. The full list names each case. The current Copilot CLI exposes no selected-model priority tier. Direct priority or fast requests return invalid_request before opening a session. flex also runs as Standard: the request is accepted and no tier is sent to the CLI. Normal requests retain the selected model, reasoning, and subscription route.

Ordinary Anthropic API

Configured reasoning effort maps to output_config.effort; unsupported model levels fail before inference. summary: "none" hides thinking deltas. Tool calls must have distinct IDs, valid object input, and names allowed by the current catalog and tool selection. Required tool selection cannot finish without a call. Outbound requests carry up to four ephemeral prompt-cache breakpoints (cache_control: { "type": "ephemeral" }): the last tool, the last system block, and the tails of the last two messages, regardless of their role. A block already marked is never marked twice, nested tool-result content never receives a marker of its own, and markers never reorder or merge caller blocks.

Only end_turn, stop_sequence, and valid caller tool_use turns complete. Paused, truncated, refused, and unknown stop reasons fail, including model_context_window_exceeded. These rules follow Anthropic's effort and stop reason contracts. The gateway does not retry or choose another billing route.

Images

User messages and caller tool results accept input_image with an inline base64 image_url. PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP signatures and encoding are validated before inference. An image is limited to 8 MiB encoded. The whole request is limited to 64 MiB, above what upstreams accept, so a long chat with many screenshots reaches the provider as it would natively and the provider's own limit applies. (Before 0.3.8 the cap was 10 MiB, which refused such chats with a 413.) Remote URLs and uploaded file IDs are rejected. The gateway does not fetch image URLs or borrow the primary account's file access.

Claude CLI prompt cache and item blocks

Each Claude inference starts the official CLI with one user message. The adapter sends each conversation item as its own content block, oldest first, and puts per-request instructions last. Earlier blocks stay byte-identical as a tool loop grows, so Claude reuses its prompt cache. In a measured three-round loop, the second and third rounds were about 98% cached; the former single-string prompt was 0% cached after the first change. Claude cache reads are reported as input_tokens_details.cached_tokens.

Each item block is plain text: a header line such as <<item 3 user>>, <<item 4 tool_call NAME ID>> or <<item 5 tool_result ID>>, the raw text, and a closing line <</item>>. A body line that starts with <<item or is <</item>> is escaped with a backslash, so item boundaries cannot be forged. The closing line matters for spend: Claude never reuses a cached prefix whose last block ends in whitespace once more blocks follow, and tool output usually ends in a newline. Without it (0.3.2 to 0.3.5), each one-shot request reused only the system and tool prefix and rewrote the whole conversation; measured on Haiku, the cached prefix stayed at 921 tokens for five rounds, and grows every round with it. This replaces the earlier JSON-escaped items, which cost 3–13% more characters. The first block is fixed text and no longer lists tool names, so a catalog change no longer rewrites it. claudeSessions.replayFormat: "json" on the Claude provider restores the JSON encoding. The format change means each active Claude chat pays one full cache write on its first request after the update.

The CLI runs with --allowedTools limited to the gateway's MCP tools, so it cannot answer a caller call itself. When Claude asks for several tools at once, every complete call reaches the caller in one response; the CLI is stopped when the API message ends, before it can act on the calls. A message cut short by max_tokens returns only the calls it completed. Output tokens come from the final message_delta, so tool turns report what was actually generated. Cancelling a request stops the CLI at once instead of waiting 1.5 seconds. A forced tool_choice keeps the full catalog, so it does not break the prompt cache; a final block names the required tool. A mismatched call ends the request without changing the catalog or automatically retrying inference.

With claudeSessions.mode: "live", the gateway instead keeps one CLI session per Codex thread, so history, thinking and the prompt cache stay native; see live Claude sessions. Live mode is the default. A mismatched call fails with a code Codex treats as final; Gateway does not retry with another catalog.

The caller's instructions and the system and developer messages before the first other message become the CLI's system prompt, after the gateway's fixed backend text, which is where Claude Code keeps its own instructions. The prompt is written to a private file and passed with --system-prompt-file, so caller text never appears in the process list. The rest of the history renders as item blocks, numbered from its first message. A later developer message stays an item in the history, and a history that holds only system and developer messages keeps them all as items. With Codex, its three leading developer messages (about 24,500 characters) moved from the user message into the system prompt.

Each Claude row's default effort is the CLI's own default for that model. Model discovery reads it without inference: after initialize, it sets the session-scoped model with apply_flag_settings and reads the applied effort from get_settings, because the initialize model list carries no default. CLI 2.1.293 reported medium for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5; high for Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6; and xhigh for Opus 4.7. The value is stored as defaultReasoningEffort in the model metadata. A model for which the CLI reports no level, or a level the row does not offer, keeps medium. Each discovery replaces the stored value, so a refresh in which the CLI reports no level, or get_settings fails, returns the row to medium.

One-shot and live CLIs both run with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL=1 and ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false, so the CLI declares only the gateway's tools (one-shot CLIs used to add two of their own). Neither inherits the host's CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_* or CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_* variables. A desktop entrypoint inherited from a Claude Code shell made each one-shot CLI send an extra post-turn summary request and print its result about 2 seconds after the turn ended. The gateway sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH to the longest caller tool description, and never below the CLI's default of 2,048 characters, so every description reaches the model whole. Before, the CLI cut longer ones at 2,048 characters.

A one-shot text turn ends at the message_delta whose stop reason is end_turn. The request completes with that message's usage, without waiting for the CLI's result. The gateway then reads the CLI's output for at most 100 ms, to keep the rate limit the CLI prints right after the turn and the context window a prompt result reports, and stops the CLI. Any other stop reason still waits for the result and keeps its error classification. Measured with CLI 2.1.293 on Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, the time from message_delta to done fell from 1.6–2.8 seconds to under 2 ms for a gateway started from a Claude Code shell, and from 4–8 ms to under 2 ms in the installed service's environment. Live sessions already received their result within 7 ms and still end there. A Fast turn also waits for the result, because only the result reports the tier served: when Claude refuses or throttles a fast request, the CLI retries at standard speed without printing a line, so the on state from its first line can be stale.

The system prompt, the item numbering, the smaller tool list and the uncut tool descriptions all change Claude's cached prefix. They ship in one release, so each active Claude chat pays one full cache write on its first request after the update. Live sessions reseed once after an inference restart anyway, so they pay that same single write.

Images on each provider route

Claude receives native image blocks through the official CLI's streamed input. Copilot receives a history item's images as file attachments on the message that owns them: the gateway writes each image (mode 0600) into the CLI's private folder, which is removed with the session, because one RPC message to the CLI is limited to 16 MiB. Tool-output images travel inline as binary results of the waiting tool call while the result stays within 12 MiB; a larger one starts the thread's session over, which sends those images as files too. Their text conversation contains labels for image ownership and order, never the image bytes. Each native harness controls its own image preprocessing. Codex and ordinary Responses upstreams retain the original image parts and detail setting. Anthropic API requests retain ordered native image blocks, including tool results. Chat Completions providers (local Qwen through vLLM) receive images only for a model whose modelMetadata lists "inputModalities": ["text", "image"]. A user message keeps its text and images in order as image_url data URLs. A tool result keeps its text in the tool message, because Chat Completions tool messages carry text only; its images follow in one user message after the run of tool results, so the results stay contiguous after the assistant's calls. A model whose metadata lists only text still refuses images with unsupported_input ("This chat model does not accept images"). The vision check in scripts/e2e-chat-compaction.mjs verifies both paths against the real model.

Model metadata carries inputModalities. The desktop adapter preserves those capabilities rather than declaring every added model text-only. Updating an older adapter executable requires a fresh launch; later catalog capability changes use the normal live refresh path.
